newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares end mixed, dollar firm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares end mixed, dollar firm.

text.p: European shares ended mixed on Wednesday, with Paris and Frankfurt higher but London lower as stronger-than-expected U.S. and British data kept concern over higher interest rates alive.
The London stock market, Europe's busiest, was more than half a percent lower after its third successive fall.
Wall Street showed a similar drop towards the end of the New York morning, led by a sell-off in high technology stocks.
On the currency market, the pound recovered some of its poise after slipping on pre-election jitters.

The dollar also made progress against the mark and the yen with a small rise in U.S. inflation boosting speculation on an increase in interest rates -- which could aid the dollar while depressing stocks and bonds. But it closed European trading below its peaks.
"The numbers, very slightly, increase the chances of the Fed raising rates next Tuesday," said Dick Howard, director of economic research at Julius Baer Investments.
Markets had focused on U.S. February consumer price data for clues on likely action at next week's meeting of the policy-making committee of the U.S. central bank, the Federal Reserve.
Many analysts expect a boost to U.S. interest rates then to keep a lid on inflation.
News that U.S. prices rose 0.3 percent last month, slightly more than market forecasts of 0.2 percent, prompted what Wall Street dealers called anticipatory selling ahead of the March 25 Fed meeting.

But Cheryl Katz, senior economist at Merrill Lynch in New York, said the price index was "slightly worse than expected ... (but) all in all, today's number, I don't think, would make the Federal Reserve tighten."

British shares had opened lower after news that Wall Street ended almost 59 points or 0.85 percent weaker on Tuesday -- more than double the 25-point loss it showed as London closed for business on Tuesday.
They then moved ahead before slipping as stronger-than-expected U.K. data revived the spectre of higher British interest rates after the general election on May 1.
"We were doing well until the figures. Now everyone is talking about inflation and an interest rate rise after the election," one London dealer said.

British January average earnings rose five percent year-on-year, versus forecasts of 4.25 percent, and retail sales climbed 0.5 percent in February and 4.4 percent year-on-year, against a predicted 0.1 and 3.6 percent.
The U.S. figures then added to the pressure.
German shares, however, advanced after February money supply data and a key business confidence survey were viewed as mildly positive signs for the economy.

M3 money growth slowed to a 9.1 percent annualised rate from the fourth 1996 quarter from January's 11.7 percent rise. The Ifo institute February German business climate index rose to 93.6 from 93.3 in January.
Steel giants Thyssen and Krupp have agreed to talk on setting up a joint steel company but their shares were still suspended after news of Krupp's hostile takeover bid.
After a two-day downward correction, French shares gained around 0.9 percent, aided by a stronger dollar -- good news for exporters -- and steady bonds.
The dollar, meanwhile, moved above 1.68 marks and 123 yen in cautious trading before slipping back from its highs.

Another gainer was the pound, hit by jitters this week after confirmation of the election date but showing a revival following the British data, including a drop in the February jobless rate to 6.2 percent from January's 6.5.
Sterling strengthened to 2.6865 marks from 2.6607 overnight and to $1.5973 from $1.5887.
Gold also revived after a sharp sell off and subsequent rally emanating largely from New York.
News that the Russian central bank planned to buy 90 tonnes of gold this year for reserves was positive, dealers said. "Anything which keeps gold off the market is mildly bullish," one said.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was quoted around 1.6808 marks and 122.59 yen, compared with Tuesday's late European levels of 1.6762 and 122.44.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 24.6 points at 4,332.2.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse floor trade 24.74 points higher at 3,315.93 but slipped to 3,305.72 in later electronic trading.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 22.82 points at 2,596.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended London trading around $348.95 an ounce, a little below its afternoon fix of $349.10 but well up from the previous London close of $346.25. Silver rose to $5.21 from $5.10.
